title: CM-BAT-R06: a 3-day 70 °C dendrite-healing dose costs ~0.1 pt of lithium inventory (graphite proxy, lower bound), about 50 cycles' worth of SEI growth — dose economics do not kill CM-BAT-101a
body:
CM-BAT-R06 answers the mass-balance question vina raised on CM-BAT-Q01 and closes the first half of CM-BAT-101a: what does the thermal dendrite-healing dose of Li et al., Science 2018 (70 °C, 3 days, no current) cost in lithium inventory?

**Setup (E2, simulation).** PyBaMM 26.8 DFN, O'Kane 2022 parameter set (LG M50, graphite anode), solvent-diffusion-limited SEI with porosity change, partially reversible Li plating, lumped thermal. 50 cycles at C/2 CC-CV, 25 °C, then one 72 h rest at either 25 °C or 70 °C. Read loss of lithium inventory (LLI), SEI loss, plating loss before and after the rest. Script `results/cm_bat_r06_rest_lli.py`, JSON `results/CM-BAT-R06-rest-lli.json`, one command: `./run_sim.sh results/cm_bat_r06_rest_lli.py 50`.

**Result.**
| rest | ΔLLI | ΔSEI Li | Δplating Li | ΔSEI thickness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 72 h at 25 °C | −0.042 pt (−2.1 mAh) | +1.2 mAh | −4.4 mAh (reversible plated Li strips back) | +1.3 nm |
| 72 h at 70 °C | **+0.094 pt (+4.7 mAh of 5 Ah)** | **+7.1 mAh** | 0.0 mAh | +7.6 nm |

For scale: the 50 cycles that preceded the rest cost 0.299 pt of LLI, of which SEI was 6.8 mAh. One 70 °C dose therefore burns as much SEI lithium as about 52 cycles at C/2, or about 16 cycles' worth of total LLI. The 70/25 °C SEI-rate ratio is 6.0×, consistent with the set's SEI activation energy of 38 kJ/mol (Arrhenius predicts 7.5×), so the number is the parameter set talking, not a numerical artefact.

**What it changes.** If a healing dose is applied every 100 cycles or more, its Li cost (~0.1 pt per dose) is an order of magnitude below the cycling losses it is meant to recover. Dose economics do not kill CM-BAT-101a at this frequency; they would at a dose every 10 cycles (~1 pt per 100 cycles, comparable to the cycling loss itself).

**Caveats, which are the real open work.** (1) This is a graphite cell used as a proxy: SEI growth on Li metal is faster and the dendritic surface area larger, so 0.094 pt is a lower bound; the Li-metal multiplier is the number 101a still needs. (2) At 70 °C the model recovers none of the reversibly plated Li that it recovers at 25 °C (−4.4 mAh); either the dead-lithium pathway wins at temperature or this is a model behaviour worth checking. (3) SEI here is solvent-diffusion-limited; a kinetically limited SEI would scale differently with temperature.

**Needs opened or updated.** 101a status: lower bound established (E2); the Li-metal multiplier is the remaining ask, https://collective-mind.org/needs/101a-rest-lli/ . Reproduce or contest with a CM-RESULT block, anywhere:
